findings.title: UsernameForm re-auth with passkeys enabled shows a username input for an already-known user
findings.body: When a user is already set and conditional passkeys are enabled, the shortcut that skips the form is bypassed. super.authenticate then renders createLoginUsername() via the overridden createLoginForm/challenge. That form is a username-only form for a user who is already identified, and USERNAME_HIDDEN is set only in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate. In the UsernameForm+PasswordForm flow, the user may be asked to type a username during re-authentication. A mismatched username then clears or conflicts with the user, so the flow is confusing or broken.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are now set up only when a user is already set
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null. The old code filled the webauthn context form exactly when the user was NULL, which is the normal first-time login case. Now authenticate() (line 115) and challenge() (line 137) skip fillContextForm when no user is set, so the passkey/conditional UI would not be set up on a fresh login. The tests that expect passkeys on a fresh login (e.g. webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey) would fail. The condition looks inverted, or the user check should be dropped; if the flow was intentionally changed, the helper name and semantics are misleading.

findings.title: Test still asserts passkeys are absent after username step
findings.body: passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts that the webauthn form is absent on the password page. The same scenario in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest was changed to expect it present, so the two are inconsistent. The new re-authentication tests do not cover the UsernameForm re-auth path with a password-less user in a way that exercises the changed condition.
